newsitem.title: FRANCE: Traders seek confirmation of Libya barley deal.
newsitem.headline: Traders seek confirmation of Libya barley deal.

text.p: European grain exporters on Wednesday said they were seeking confirmation of market talk Libya had bought optional-origin feed barley.
Several exporters said Libya might have bought 200,000 tonnes of barley in bulk and 100,000 tonnes in bags but stressed this was yet to be confirmed.
"I heard that they bought and that it was cheap," one exporter said.
One exporter cited a selling price of $125 per tonne, Fob.
Exporters stressed that business with Libya was hard to track down and that contract finalisation usually hinged on securing the proper letters of credit.
In December traders said Libya was in the market to import optional-origin barley and was asking for prices. These rumors surfaced again last week.
In its latest report the International Grains Council (IGC) forecast Libya may import 300,000 tonnes of barley in the 1996/97 season.
